extracted.intended_audience: mathematical researchers, prospective MFO participants, institute staff and stakeholders (funders, librarians, editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the Institute's programmatic goals, publication series scopes, library and infrastructure policies, and training/program formats described in the MFO 2015 annual report. Useful for understanding eligibility, scope, and editorial/operational standards at Oberwolfach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary workshop goal (Kadison–Singer Arbeitsgemeinschaft)
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of this Arbeitsgemeinschaft was to bring together people from each of these fields to support interactions between these areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the majority of the talks centered around topics in polynomial geometry, combinatorics, and real algebraic geometry, participants came from areas such as harmonic analysis, convex geometry, and frame theory. Implied program criterion: select topics and participants to foster cross-field interaction around the central problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory workshop design (Mathematical Quasicrystals)
rubrics_metrics.description: This introductory workshop encouraged participants to read important recent works in the topology, geometry and dynamics of highly regular (but aperiodic) discrete sets in Euclidean spaces, and their corresponding tiling spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize preparatory reading, present multiple perspectives (topology, mathematical physics, dynamics, diophantine approximation, discrete mathematics), and focus sessions to expose participants to different viewpoints on a shared topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar topical scope and balance (Shapes and Patterns seminar)
rubrics_metrics.description: The seminar provided an introduction to analytical and numerical techniques for dealing with shapes and patterns observed in physical or biological systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include analysis of relaxation phenomena, shape optimisation, pattern selection, energy scaling laws, phase field and sharp interface approaches, and mathematical models for interplay between shape and patterns in biological systems. Implied guideline: combine analytical theory and numerical simulation; cover both modelling and applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library access and collection policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The library is a reference library available to the Institute’s guests 24 hours a day and is a central working tool for scientific research at Oberwolfach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory (end of 2015): approx. 57,870 books, approx. 30,500 bound journal volumes, ~5,000 dissertations, 540 current printed journal subscriptions, ~5,000 licensed electronic journals. Participation in the Südwestdeutschen Bibliotheksverbund (SWB) and use of BSZ-provided software for cataloging. Notes on sustainability: rising journal prices threaten the level of service; continued provision has depended on donations and foundation support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional IT and support staffing standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Information technology and administrative support are important for scientific work and worldwide communication; the Institute provided approximately 25 positions across scientific administration, library, IT, guest services and housekeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT supports electronic publications, databases and mathematical software as well as email and internet services. Support staff and on-site boarding/catering/guest services are considered essential background infrastructure to guarantee efficient, concentrated work for visiting researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access policy of the MFO
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFO supports the idea of Open Access. Hence, all publications are electronically freely available on the website www.mfo.de (with the exception of the book series Oberwolfach Seminars at Birkhäuser).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers/series exceptions should be noted; the Institute aims to make output available openly when possible and indicates where restrictions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Reports (OWR) publication scope
rubrics_metrics.description: OWR is published in cooperation with the EMS publishing house and contains extended abstracts of the talks in the Workshops, Mini-Workshops and Arbeitsgemeinschaften.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: document and disseminate extended abstracts of workshop talks. Example: 2015 issues OWR 12.1–12.4 published (more than 3,600 pages total). Editorial/format implication: OWR expects extended abstracts rather than full papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Seminars (OWS) book series scope
rubrics_metrics.description: OWS is a book series in cooperation with the Birkhäuser Verlag (Basel) that makes the content of the Oberwolfach Seminars accessible to doctoral students, postdoctoral researchers and interested researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function/target audience: educational monographs based on seminar content. Note the exception to the general Open Access statement: OWS is published commercially via Birkhäuser; in 2015 one OWS title was published (vol. 46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oberwolfach Preprints (OWP) scope and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: In OWP results of longer-term research stays (RiP and OWLF) are published, but this can also include an Oberwolfach Lecture or selected mathematical talks given at the MFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OWP serves to publish research results related to longer visits and selected talks; 2015 included a numbered list of OWP items (e.g., 'Euler Reflexion Formulas for Motivic Multiple Zeta Functions', 'Noncommutative Marked Surfaces', etc.). Implied editorial guideline: OWP accepts preprints arising from longer stays and special presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snapshots of modern mathematics outreach guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Snapshots explain mathematical ideas and problems in an accessible way; they are written by participants of the scientific program and edited by a team of editors for a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Snapshots are published freely under a Creative Commons license on the MFO website and imaginary.org; the project is funded (Klaus Tschira Stiftung, Oberwolfach Foundation, MFO). Implied editorial criteria: clarity, accessibility, editorial polishing, and outreach orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leibniz Fellows program aim and eligibility principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Leibniz Fellows program (introduced 2007) supports outstanding young mathematicians in the realization of their own research projects during an important period of their scientific career and offers undisturbed working conditions with excellent infrastructure in an international environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program implication: selection targets 'outstanding' postdoctoral researchers with independent research projects; the Institute provides infrastructure and sometimes external guest researchers; examples include named fellows and visiting guest researchers with specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training weeks and professional development target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute hosts training and professional development events targeted to well-defined audiences (e.g., final training week for especially gifted German pupils preparing for the IMO; a Fortbildungsveranstaltung for librarians on E-Science Baden-Württemberg focusing on research data management and Open Access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event design should match the audience: IMO training focuses on preparing top pupils for competition; librarian training emphasized research data management, repositories, data management plans, data citation, Green Open Access, data flows, acquisition profiles, secondary publication rights, and virtual research environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research in Pairs (RiP) program format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research in Pairs program hosts pairs (or small groups) of researchers for focused collaborative stays; the 2015 section lists participating researchers and their visit dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program outputs often feed into OWP publications; implied operational criteria include specified visit durations, assigned dates, and the expectation of collaborative research productivity during the stay.
